To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bacterial and fungal communities are different across land-water interfaces in tallgrass prairie ecosystems, and woody plant removal impacts bacterial and fungal community composition.
woody plant removal impacts bacterial and fungal communities in a tallgrass stream ecosystem, but the magnitude of these effects is less than the influence of land-water interface.
woody plant removal in a grassland ecosystem impacts bacterial and fungal communities in stream sediments and adjacent soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impacts of woedy plant encroachment on grassland soil microbial communities.
the effects of woody plant encroaching into grassland ecosystems and how the removal of these woody plants impacts the soil microbial community.
the effects of woody plant encroaching and removal on soil bacterial and fungal communities in grassland streams and adjacent uplands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
woody plant encroached areas have a different soil microbial community than areas where woody vegetation has been removed.

woody plant encroached areas had greater relative abundance of cyanobacteria, ascomycota, chytridomycota and glomeromycota, while removal areas had greater relative abundances of planctomycetes, basidiomycota, and cyanobacteria.
the woody plant encroached areas had a lower fungal diversity than the removal area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
woody vegetation removal in grassland ecosystems has the potential to alter bacterial and fungal communities in both terrestrial and aquatic habitats.
woody plant encroached grassland restoration impacts soil microbial communities in ways we do not understand.

riparian woody encroached areas had a greater impact on bacterial communities than fungal communities and that bacterial community composition was more influenced by distance from streams than fungal community composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
woody plant encroached areas have different microbial communities than removal areas and this likely has consequences for plant health.
woody plant removal impacts microbial communities in both the terrestrial and aquatic habitats of grasslands.

woody encroached riparian zones are likely to have different microbial community structure and composition from grassland riparian zones and these changes may be more pronounced for bacteria than fungi.
